intro: Wuhan rewards visitors with river views, spicy hot dry noodles and a fast-growing metro. Pick how long you have and what you enjoy most.
tour_note: Check the tour page for which entry tickets are included.

notes: Metro: 12 lines, 300+ stations; Line 2 links the airport and Hankou station, Line 4 links Wuhan and Wuchang stations.
Metro fares are distance-based; a Wuhan Tong card costs ¥15 and gives about 10% off rides, buses and ferries.
Buses: ¥1-2 flat fare (¥0.8-1.6 with card); Alipay and WeChat QR codes work on many routes.
Taxis are cheap and metered; ride-hailing apps like DiDi work well, Uber does not operate in China.
Two streetcar systems serve Hanyang and the Guanggu area.
Ferries cross the Yangtze between the three towns; walking and shared bikes suit short hops.

yellow_crane_tower.name: Yellow Crane Tower
yellow_crane_tower.price_text: ≈ CNY 70 entry; check on the day
yellow_crane_tower.tip: Climb to the top floor for the Yangtze and bridge view, and go early to beat tour groups.

hubei_museum.name: Hubei Provincial Museum
hubei_museum.price_text: Free with advance booking; some special shows charged
hubei_museum.tip: Book a free slot online in advance and head straight for the bronze bells and Chu relics.

han_river.name: Han River, China
han_river.tip: Walk the Hanyang bank near the confluence at sunset, then stay for the lit bridges.

greenland_center.name: Wuhan Greenland Center
greenland_center.price_text: Exterior free; observation access varies — check on the day
greenland_center.hours: Tower visible at all hours; interior access varies
greenland_center.tip: Best seen from across the river or the riverside promenade rather than up close.

hubu_alley.name: Hubu Alley snack street
hubu_alley.price_text: Pay per stall; small dishes a few CNY each
hubu_alley.hours: Busiest roughly 10:00–21:00; some stalls close earlier
hubu_alley.tip: Try hot dry noodles (reganmian) and doupi; carry small cash or use a phone payment app.

jiqing_street.name: Jiqing Street food street
jiqing_street.tip: Come hungry for crayfish and skewers; it is liveliest after dark.

jianghan_walk.name: Jianghan Road and Bund walk
jianghan_walk.tip: Walk from the old customs buildings along the Bund to the river for colonial-era architecture.

east_lake.name: East Lake Greenway
east_lake.hours: Open all day; bike hire daytime hours
east_lake.tip: Rent a bike and ride a stretch of the greenway; it is long, so pick one section.

yangtze_cruise.name: Yangtze night cruise
yangtze_cruise.price_text: ≈ CNY 100–200 depending on boat — check on the day
yangtze_cruise.tip: Book a riverside departure and sit on deck for the lit bridges and skyline.

guqing_street.name: Guqing Street coffee lane
guqing_street.price_text: Pay per cafe; a coffee is a few tens of CNY
guqing_street.tip: A short lane of small cafes and old buildings — good for a slow afternoon wander.

optics_valley.name: Optics Valley pedestrian street
optics_valley.price_text: Free to walk; shops and food extra
optics_valley.tip: A modern shopping and food area near the universities; combine with East Lake.

guiyuan_temple.name: Guiyuan Temple
guiyuan_temple.price_text: Small entry fee — check on the day
guiyuan_temple.tip: A working Buddhist temple; dress modestly and keep voices low.

wuhan_university.name: Wuhan University campus walk
wuhan_university.price_text: Free; campus access rules vary — check on the day
wuhan_university.tip: Famous for cherry blossoms in spring; check visitor access rules before you go.

hot_dry_noodles.name: Hot dry noodles breakfast (reganmian)
hot_dry_noodles.price_text: A bowl is a few CNY
hot_dry_noodles.tip: Wuhan's classic breakfast — eat it early at a local noodle shop.

yangtze_bridge.name: Wuhan Yangtze River Bridge walk
yangtze_bridge.tip: Walk the lower deck path across the river for wide views; allow time for the length.

hankou_old_concession.name: Hankou old concession streets
hankou_old_concession.tip: Wander the side streets behind the Bund for old bank buildings and quiet cafes.

qingchuan_pavilion.name: Qingchuan Pavilion riverside
qingchuan_pavilion.price_text: Small fee for the pavilion — check on the day
qingchuan_pavilion.tip: A quiet riverside spot with a view over the confluence; good with a Han River walk.

wuchang_riverside.name: Wuchang riverside promenade
wuchang_riverside.tip: Evening walk with locals along the Yangtze; combine with the Yellow Crane Tower area.

stays.why: Historic concession streets, big malls and easy metro links; good base for food and nightlife.
Closest to Yellow Crane Tower, the Hubei Museum and East Lake; handy for Wuchang station.
Quieter and cheaper; good for Guiyuan Temple and ferry hops across the Yangtze.
Modern area near East Lake and universities; suits tech-minded travelers and longer stays.

food: Start the day like a local: hot dry noodles (reganmian), a sesame-paste noodle dish, usually ¥5–10 a bowl.
Try doupi (sticky rice and egg pancake) and mianwo rice cakes at breakfast stalls; cheap and filling.
Snack streets: Hubu Alley near Yellow Crane Tower and Jiqing Street in Hankou for evening food.
Wuhan food is spicy and river-based; ask for less chili (bu la) if you need it.
Street stalls are cheapest; sit-down restaurants run about ¥40–100 per person. Check hygiene with your eyes.
more_time: Add a day for East Lake: rent a bike and ride the greenway; allow 3–4 hours.
Take the ferry across the Yangtze for a cheap river crossing and skyline views.
Day trip to Guiyuan Temple in Hanyang for a quieter half-day.
